title: jól / rosszul + tud: How Well You Can Do Something

sections.title: Grading a skill
sections.content: You already know jól ("well") and rosszul ("badly") from earlier units. Drop one in right before tud and you can grade a skill instead of just claiming or denying it — the adverb describes tud itself, so it sits directly in front of the conjugated verb, before the infinitive.

sections.title: Word order: adverb + tud + infinitive
rows: I'm not a good driver. (lit. I drive badly.)
We're pretty bad at playing the piano.

items.spanish: Ildikó nagyon jól tud főzni, Gábor rosszul.
items.english: Ildikó cooks very well; Gábor cooks badly.
How well can you speak Hungarian?

sections.content: nagyon and elég work the same way in front of jól/rosszul as you already know: nagyon jól (very well), elég rosszul (pretty badly) — they stack in front of the adverb, which stays in front of tud.
